knowledge:
- key_parameters: X=Raw UMI count matrix where rows represent genes and columns represent cells. Normalization or imputation should not be applied beforehand ;; batch_label=Vector of characters indicating batch labels of cells (set to NULL for single-batch datasets) ;; method=Method for feature gene selection, such as "wds" (working dispersion score) ;; nfeature=Number of feature genes to select (e.g., 500) ;; cand_lab_df=Data frame of candidate cell labels where each row is a cell and each column is a set of labels ;; cell_size_factor=Size factors of cells, calculated using the size_factor function ;; cdi_type=Type of CDI metric to plot, either "CDI_AIC" (suggested for selecting optimal subtypes) or "CDI_BIC" (suggested for selecting optimal main cell types)
- alternatives: Candidate label sets are typically generated using external clustering methods such as K-Means or Seurat, which CDI then evaluates to find the optimal clustering resolution or method.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have generated multiple candidate clustering label sets (e.g., from different algorithms or different resolution parameters) on scRNA-seq UMI count data and want a statistically principled way to select the optimal clustering.
- pitfalls: Do not use normalized or imputed data as input, because CDI models raw UMI counts ;; Ensure that the column names of the candidate label data frame are formatted as "[ClusteringMethod]_k[NumberOfClusters]" (e.g., "KMeans_k5") so calculate_CDI can automatically extract the clustering method, or provide it via the clustering_method argument ;; Ensure that the correct CDI metric is used: CDI-BIC is preferred for main cell types because it penalizes model complexity more heavily, while CDI-AIC is preferred for fine-grained subtypes.

workflows.name: single_batch_cdi
workflows.intent: Select the optimal clustering label set for a single-batch scRNA-seq dataset using CDI.
input: one_batch_matrix_label_df (data frame of candidate cell labels)
one_batch_matrix_celltype (optional vector of benchmark cell types)
workflows.stages: 1. Select feature genes using feature_gene_selection ;; 2. Calculate cell size factors using size_factor ;; 3. Calculate CDI for candidate labels using calculate_CDI ;; 4. Visualize CDI values using CDI_lineplot ;; 5. (Optional) Compare optimal labels with benchmark labels using contingency_heatmap ;; 6. (Optional) Calculate CDI for benchmark labels and add to the lineplot
workflows.code:
feature_gene_indx <- feature_gene_selection(
	X = one_batch_matrix, 
	batch_label = NULL, 
	method = "wds", 
	nfeature = 500)
sub_one_batch_matrix <- one_batch_matrix[feature_gene_indx,]

one_batch_matrix_size_factor <- size_factor(X = one_batch_matrix)

start_time <- Sys.time()
CDI_return1 <- calculate_CDI(
	X = sub_one_batch_matrix, 
	cand_lab_df = one_batch_matrix_label_df, 
	batch_label = NULL, 
	cell_size_factor = one_batch_matrix_size_factor)
end_time <- Sys.time()
print(difftime(end_time, start_time))

CDI_lineplot(cdi_dataframe = CDI_return1, cdi_type = "CDI_BIC")

contingency_heatmap(benchmark_label = one_batch_matrix_celltype,
	candidate_label = one_batch_matrix_label_df$KMeans_k5,
	rename_candidate_clusters = TRUE,
	candidate_cluster_names = paste0('cluster', seq_len(length(unique(one_batch_matrix_label_df$KMeans_k5)))))

benchmark_return1 <- calculate_CDI(X = sub_one_batch_matrix,
	cand_lab_df = one_batch_matrix_celltype, 
	batch_label = NULL, 
	cell_size_factor = one_batch_matrix_size_factor)

CDI_lineplot(cdi_dataframe = CDI_return1,
	cdi_type = "CDI_BIC",
	benchmark_celltype_cdi = benchmark_return1,
	benchmark_celltype_ncluster = length(unique(one_batch_matrix_celltype)))

workflows.name: multi_batch_cdi
workflows.intent: Select the optimal clustering label set for a multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset using CDI.
input: two_batch_matrix_label_df (data frame of candidate cell labels)
two_batch_matrix_celltype (optional vector of benchmark cell types)
workflows.stages: 1. Select feature genes using feature_gene_selection with batch labels ;; 2. Calculate cell size factors using size_factor ;; 3. Calculate CDI for candidate labels using calculate_CDI with batch labels ;; 4. (Optional) Calculate CDI for benchmark labels ;; 5. Visualize CDI values using CDI_lineplot ;; 6. (Optional) Compare optimal labels with benchmark labels using contingency_heatmap
workflows.code:
feature_gene_indx <- feature_gene_selection(
	X = two_batch_matrix,
	batch_label = two_batch_matrix_batch,
	method = "wds",
	nfeature = 500)
sub_two_batch_matrix <- two_batch_matrix[feature_gene_indx,]

two_batch_matrix_size_factor <- size_factor(two_batch_matrix)

start_time <- Sys.time()
CDI_return2 <- calculate_CDI(
	X = sub_two_batch_matrix,
	cand_lab_df = two_batch_matrix_label_df, 
	batch_label = two_batch_matrix_batch,
	cell_size_factor = two_batch_matrix_size_factor)
end_time <- Sys.time()
print(difftime(end_time, start_time))

benchmark_return <- calculate_CDI(
	X = sub_two_batch_matrix,
	cand_lab_df = two_batch_matrix_celltype,
	batch_label = two_batch_matrix_batch,
	cell_size_factor = two_batch_matrix_size_factor)

CDI_lineplot(cdi_dataframe = CDI_return2,
	cdi_type = "CDI_BIC",
	benchmark_celltype_cdi = benchmark_return,
	benchmark_celltype_ncluster = length(unique(two_batch_matrix_celltype))) 

contingency_heatmap(
	benchmark_label = two_batch_matrix_celltype,
	candidate_label = two_batch_matrix_label_df$Seurat_k5,
	rename_candidate_clusters = TRUE,
	candidate_cluster_names = paste0('cluster', seq_len(length(unique(one_batch_matrix_label_df$Seurat_k5)))))
